claims.claim_text: When President Obama took office, the United States was experiencing its worst economic downturn since the Great Depression.
During the month President Obama took office, 800,000 Americans lost jobs, more than in any single month during the preceding sixty years.
On his first day in office, President Obama acted immediately to stop the economic free fall and put Americans back to work.
President Obama and Democrats characterized American workers as tougher than tough economic times.
Since early 2010, the U.S. private sector had created 4.5 million jobs.
Rebuilding genuine middle-class security cannot be achieved solely through spending cuts.

The United States needs an economy producing future jobs and goods bought abroad, rather than one built on outsourcing or loopholes or on risky financial deals that jeopardize everyone, especially the middle class.
